texts.facts: This Judgment shall decide the present appeal filed by the appellant No.1 company and other individual working in it viz. appellant Nos. 2 to 4 under Section 76 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 as amended upto date (hereinafter referred as 'FSS Act') assailing impugned order dated 02.06.2021 passed by the Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate (District East), Delhi, whereby the appellant have been convicted under Section 23(1), 26(1), 26(2)(ii), 27(1), 27(2)(c), 27(3)(c) read with Section 3(1)(zF) (C)(i) of the FSS Act and also for violation of Regulation No. 2.2.1.5, 2.2.1.7 and 2.2.210 of the Food Safety & Standards (Packaging & Labeling) Regulation, 2011 (hereinafter referred as FSS (P&L) Regulations) besides the importer respondent no. 6 for being found in violation of Section 25(1) (i) of FSS Act and thereby each of the individual appellant Nos. 2 and 4 have been sentenced to pay penalty of Rs. 10,000/ whereas appellant No. 3 has been sentenced to pay find of Rs. 20,000/, while the appellant No.1 company has been imposed with fine of Rs.30,000/ as also Sh. Abhishek Jain and M/s. Topnotch Retail Pvt. Ltd., respondent no. 5 & 6 respectively who have been imposed with fine of Rs.30,000/ each with directions to pay the penalty amount within 15 days of the order. BRIEF FACTS: 2. Briefly stated, the appeal was filed on 15.07.2021 and it is within the period of limitation as prescribed in Rule 3.3.1 (2) of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011. The case as brought out in the appeal is that appellant No.4 Bipin Kumar Maurya is the FBO/Assistant Restaurant Manager in one of the outlet of Pizza Hut (Devyani International Ltd.) situated at G48, V3S Mall, Plot No.10, District Central, Laxmi Nagar, Delhi110096; and that the appellant No.2 Sh. Pradeep Kumar is the nominee of the said outlet whereas appellant No.3 Arun Kumar is the nominee of the Warehouse of the company situated at W111, Gurgaon Dry Warehouse, Plot No. 18, Sector35, Gurugaon122004 whereas appellant No.1 M/s. Devyani International Ltd. is a company duly incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 having its corporate office at Plot No.18, Sector3, Gurugram, Haryana. It is stated that the appellant No.1 is engaged in the 'Food & Beverages Industry' and holds impeccable reputation for its tinge free track records having more than 500 outlets in various parts of India. 3. It is stated that on 21.06.2018 at about 3.30 p.m. the complainant Ms. Anjali, Food Safety Officer (FSO) inspected the store of appellant No.1 company after disclosing her identity to FBO/ Vendor i.e., the appellant No.4 and she purchased "Fusilli Barilli (Pasta)" i.e., a sampled commodity on payment of Rs. 360/ towards the cost of the sample vide credit notice receipt dated 21.06.2018, which consisted for 4X500 gms of "Fusilli Barilli (Pasta)" taken in the original sealed condition of the same batch having identical main label declaration; and that sample commodity were divided in four equal parts and sealed as per law. To cut the long story short, after conducting the proceedings at the spot, one counter part of the sample was forwarded to the Food Analyst, Delhi for analysis, M/S. Devyani International Ltd vs State on 24 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25667495/ 2 who vide his report No. FSS/1028/2018 dated 04.07.2018 opined that sample is "misbranded" because there is violation of Regulation No. 2.2.1.5, 2.2.1.7 and 2.2.2.(10) of the FSS(P & L) Regulations. Accordingly, the Food Safety Officer filed a complaint and the matter came to be decided by the Adjudicating Officer/ADM vide impugned order dated 02.06.2021, the details of which have already been described hereinabove. GROUNDS OF APPEAL: 4. The impugned order dated 02.06.2021 is assailed inter alia on the ground that the complaint is barred by limitation in terms of Section 77 of the FSS Act as cognizance has been taken by the Adjudicating Officer/ADM much after expiry of one year from the date of commission of the alleged offence, for which reliance is placed on the decision in the case of Dayachand v. The State of Madhya Pradesh, 2017 (1) FAC 253 and Pankaj Mahajan v. State of Himachal Pradesh, decided on 26.04.2017; and it is assailed on the ground that the Adjudicating Officer/ADM failed to appreciate that the appellants had purchased the sampled commodity from M/s. Topnotch Retail Pvt. Ltd., 308, Best Sky Tower, Plot No. F5, Netaji Subhash Place, Pitampura, Delhi110034 (Imported and Marketed Company) i.e. the respondent No.6 in the main complaint vide invoice No. TN/028/201819 dated 10.04.2018 in sealed condition; and that appellants had no concern with the label declaration; and that the appellants were rather bonafide consumers of the product and had taken all necessary due diligence before purchasing the sampled commodity . Reliance is placed on the decision by the Hon'ble Judge of the Nagpur Bench in Criminal Application No. 2871 of 2004 decided on 07.01.2008 and reported in All M.R. 2008 (1) Page NO. 701 besides P. Unnikrishanan v. Food Inspector, Palghat Municipality Kerla, State, 1996(I) EFR 397 (SC); and it is further assailed as the ground that the Adjudicating Officer/ADM failed to appreciate that that the appellants are protected by guarantee as enumerated in Section 80(B) (2)(d) (I) of the FSS Act; and that the guarantee as provided in Section 26(4) of the FSS Act for which reliance is placed on the decision in the case of M/s. Apsara Biscuit Company v Dr. P.M. Kothekar (FSO), FSAT Appeal No. 16/2013 and 17/2013; and that the Adjudicating Officer/ADM passed the impugned order in a mechanical manner and the appellants cannot be held criminally responsible or liable for misbrand of the sample commodity, and therefore, no offence has been committed by the appellants. 5. On filing of the appeal, the operation of impugned order was stayed vide order dated 15.07.2021, subject to the appellants furnishing a DD/FDR/Bank Guarantee to the amount equivalent to the fine imposed by the Adjudicating Officer/ADM, which has been complied with. Notice of the present appeal was issued to the respondent and the entire record of the ADM has been produced. A reply has been filed by the respondent and the appeal is opposed.
texts.arguments: There is no merit in the plea by the Ld. Chief PP for the respondent that it was a case of direct sale since the term 'sale' is defined by Section 3 (zr) of the FSS Act "to mean sale of any article of food, whether for cash or on credit or by way of exchange and whether by wholesale or retail for human consumption or use". 11.
texts.petitioner_arguments: There is no merit in the plea by the Ld. Chief PP for the respondent that it was a case of direct sale since the term 'sale' is defined by Section 3 (zr) of the FSS Act "to mean sale of any article of food, whether for cash or on credit or by way of exchange and whether by wholesale or retail for human consumption or use". 11.
